title: author a reusable wargame-a-component skill from the AI-wargaming research (durable red-team capability)
description:
Operationalizes the 2026-07-12 AI-wargaming research brief into a durable, reusable team capability — the user's stated goal of 'mejorar cómo se usa fable y mejorar búsqueda de patrones'. This wargame session (TASK-140..146) was run manually; this skill makes the method repeatable for the 'later pass over everything' the user asked for.

Create `.claude/skills/wargame-a-component/SKILL.md` (+ any plugin-root parity copy per the repo's skill convention) capturing the research's step-by-step protocol, with references/ splitting the attack taxonomy for progressive disclosure. The method (verbatim from the brief):
1. Name the component + its trust boundaries (every untrusted→trusted crossing).
2. Assign roles: Control (orchestrator), Red (a subagent briefed with the cited attack taxonomy), Blue (the REAL shipped pipeline, run for real — the single most important rule: Blue executes actual gate code / real CLI calls / real subagent spawns, never a tabletop description), optional White cell (note-taker).
3. Seed 1 inject per trust boundary from a CITED taxonomy, not improvised.
4. Run rounds: Red proposes a concrete artifact → Blue processes it through the actual code path → Control adjudicates caught/missed/partial and records WHICH gate was responsible.
5. Adapt: after each round Red tries to evade whatever caught it last round.
6. Stop condition: N rounds / taxonomy exhausted / time-box.
7. Convert every 'Red wins' outcome into a tdd ticket whose AC = 'replaying this exact inject is now caught', with the inject artifact attached as the test fixture.
8. Feed the round log back as detection signal (new evasion patterns → new scanner rules/fixtures — the src/skill-scan.js loop, see TASK-141).
9. Re-run the same inject set after fixes land as a regression pass.

references/ should carry: (a) the supply-chain / third-party-skill inject taxonomy (credential exfil, command exec, data-routing, persistence into .claude/settings.json hooks, Unicode-tag injection U+E0000–U+E007F, DDIPE, typosquatting, license spoofing, indirect injection via fetched content, and the 91% injection+malware co-occurrence) with source URLs; (b) the 'useless vs valuable wargame' checklist; (c) a note that severity scoring should reuse the repo's existing reviewer HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW convention (the LLM-wargame literature is qualitative — no numeric rubric to import). The frontmatter description must state WHEN to load it (progressive disclosure) so Fable can decide relevance.

verification_tier uat-only (skill authoring / docs; no source logic). Verify by running the skill's own protocol against ONE small component as a smoke test and confirming it produces a caught/missed finding + a replayable fixture.
acceptance_criteria: .claude/skills/wargame-a-component/SKILL.md exists with progressive-disclosure frontmatter (a description stating WHEN to load it) and the 9-step protocol above in the body; references/ split out the attack taxonomy + the useless-vs-valuable checklist.

The skill explicitly encodes the two load-bearing rules from the research: Blue plays the REAL shipped pipeline (never a tabletop description), and every 'Red wins' outcome becomes a tdd ticket with the inject as a replayable test fixture.

The supply-chain inject taxonomy in references/ carries the cited source URLs (OWASP ASI02, Snyk/ToxicSkills, CSA SKILL.md briefing, arXiv:2510.26328, reversec 'Skill Issues', MalSkillBench) so injects are seeded from cited attacks, not improvised.

A smoke-test UAT: run the skill's protocol against one small component (candidate: re-run the A6 skill-scan wargame from TASK-141) and confirm it yields at least one caught/missed finding plus a replayable fixture, recorded as the uat comment.

Skill-parity + doc-lock/skill-listing sensors green; npm run test:all green. If this skill should also be surfaced in orchestrator-routing or a command, that wiring is either done or explicitly deferred with a note.

comments.author: uat
comments.body:
UAT (AC4 smoke test — verified by Orchestrator; uat_delegated_to_orchestrator). Dogfooded the newly-authored wargame-a-component skill by running its 9-step protocol against a FRESH small component (not the already-wargamed skill-scan), proving the method yields a real caught/missed finding + a replayable fixture.

Target: src/license-detect.js. Trust boundary: an untrusted skill's own files → license classification → the assimilation approval package.
Roles: Control = Orchestrator; Red = inject seeded from references/attack-taxonomy.md's 'license-field spoofing'; Blue = the REAL detectLicense + classifyLicense pipeline (run via node harness, per the 'Blue plays the real shipped pipeline, never a tabletop' load-bearing rule).
Red inject (concrete artifact): a skillDir with a forged `// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT` header in helper.js WHILE the real LICENSE file is GNU GPL v3.
Blue result (real execution): detectLicense → spdx_id='MIT', detected_via='spdx-header'; classifyLicense → 'permissive'. The GPL-3.0 LICENSE file was never consulted (Step 1 header precedence).
Control adjudication: RED WINS (a MISS) — the responsible gate is detectLicense's fallback-chain ordering. Impact bounded (license is decision-support only; TASK-140 still requires a security-reviewer 'safe' to approve), but it feeds the human a false-clean license verdict.
Protocol step 7 applied: the Red-win was converted to a tdd ticket (TASK-150) with the exact inject described as the replayable fixture.

AC4 PASS: the protocol produced >=1 caught/missed finding (a MISS) plus a replayable fixture (TASK-150 carries it), executing the real pipeline, seeded from the cited taxonomy — exactly what the skill prescribes. The method demonstrably works and immediately surfaced a genuine (bounded) finding on its first fresh target.
